content: The medication is indicated for the treatment of bile acid synthesis disorders caused by single-enzyme defects (SEDs) at a dosage of 10-15 mg/kg/day, administered orally once daily or divided into two doses per day. It is also indicated as an adjunctive treatment for peroxisomal disorders (PDs), including Zellweger spectrum disorders, in patients presenting with liver disease, steatorrhea, or complications arising from reduced absorption of fat-soluble vitamins. The safety and efficacy of this treatment for extrahepatic manifestations of bile acid synthesis disorders due to SEDs or PDs have not been established. For patients under 3 weeks of age, the safety and efficacy of this treatment have not been established. For patients aged 3 weeks or older, the recommended dosage is 10-15 mg/kg/day, administered orally once daily or divided into two doses per day. Drug Interactions: 1. Atazanavir: Increases the toxicity of cholic acid by reducing its elimination. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative medications. If co-administration is necessary, monitor serum transaminases and bilirubin levels closely. 2. Felodipine: Increases cholic acid toxicity by decreasing its elimination. Avoid concurrent use or use an alternative drug. Monitor liver function tests if co-administration is unavoidable. 3. Aluminum Hydroxide: Reduces the effectiveness of cholic acid by binding to it in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer cholic acid at least 1 hour before or 4-6 hours after taking aluminum-based antacids. 4. Atorvastatin: Increases cholic acid toxicity by reducing its elimination. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid concurrent use of bile salt efflux pump (BSEP) inhibitors, as they may exacerbate the accumulation of conjugated bile salts in the liver, leading to clinical symptoms. 5.
